Just a little thing on the practically infinite variety of the cosmos. Astronomy has discovered a fair few planets outside of our own system since the introduction of various orbiting telescopes, but this one in particular is rather noteworthy.

For you see, aside from the usual chemical deathworldiness that characterises a great many planets, this one has remarkably Earthlike weather patterns and precipitation, save for one thing.

Because on this planet, it does not rain H2O, it rains silicon dioxide, superheated by the atmosphere to the point of becoming liquid. Moreover, the exceptionally high wind speeds on this planet are such as to completely sweep any precipitation into a very lateral vector, with minimal downward motion.

In other words, it rains molten glass sideways.

And you wonder why space is scary.

TLDR: there is a planet in this universe where it rains molten glass sideways, and the fact that this is possible should really drive home the point of how the cosmos can be plain freaky sometimes.
